JNJ.rationale: JNJ presents a mixed but slightly positive fundamental picture. On the positive side, the company delivered solid Q2 2026 results with revenue of $25.31B (+6.6% YoY) and beat consensus estimates on both revenue and EPS ($2.90 adjusted vs $2.85 est). The Innovative Medicine segment grew 7.8% YoY with strong oncology performance (Darzalex +19%, Tremfya +73%). Management raised full-year guidance to $100.8-101.4B revenue and $11.60-11.75 adjusted EPS. The company has a strong balance sheet with $20.76B cash, maintains 64 consecutive years of dividend increases, and is targeting $100B in annual revenue for the first time. However, several headwinds temper enthusiasm: (1) GAAP net income was essentially flat YoY at $5.53B despite revenue growth, suggesting margin pressure; (2) the P/E of ~29.7x is near the top of its 365-day range (17.6-31.1x), having expanded from ~17.6x a year ago — the stock is no longer cheap; (3) Stelara biosimilar competition is a significant headwind (sales down 56%); (4) the talc litigation remains an overhang despite a proposed $5.5B settlement; (5) rising 10-year Treasury yields (4.68%) and elevated corporate bond yields (6.32%) create a less favorable backdrop for defensive yield plays. The stock has already rallied +12.5% in the last quarter and +28% YTD, suggesting much of the good news is priced in. The near-term catalyst of the Q2 earnings beat and guidance raise has already been delivered (July 15), limiting further re-rating potential. Net: solid franchise with good trajectory, but valuation has expanded significantly and limits upside from here.
